quickAnswer: West Boylston's median home was built in 1964 (9th-oldest of the 50 towns we serve), and its median owner-occupied value is $382,400, 49th of 50. Oil (41.0%) and utility gas (39.4%) are nearly tied, and a municipal utility serves the town.
body: ## A 1964 housing stock at some of the lowest values on our list

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) puts the median West Boylston home at 1964 and the median owner-occupied value at $382,400. The first is the 9th-oldest median on our list of 50 towns, the second the 49th-highest value, against $579,150 for the middle town.

Of 2,930 housing units, 1,972 (67.3%) were built before 1980, the 11th-highest share, against 57.2% for the middle town. The largest single band is 1940 to 1959, with 851 homes (29.0%). Another 497 (17.0%) go back to 1939 or earlier, 624 (21.3%) to 1960 to 1979 and 357 (12.2%) to 1980 to 1999. Newer homes are a real minority, but not a tiny one: 601 (20.5%) date from 2000 on, and 267 (9.1%) from 2010 on.
## A split down the middle: oil against gas

In West Boylston the two main fuels are nearly tied. Fuel oil heats 1,173 occupied homes (41.0%) and utility gas heats 1,128 (39.4%). Electricity heats 292 (10.2%), bottled or tank gas 148 (5.2%) and wood 80 (2.8%). Oil sits a little above the middle town's 36.5% and gas a little below its 41.9%.

That balance means two comparison paths are both live at replacement time. A home on gas can usually be replaced with a new gas system, while an oil home can look at a gas conversion if a main is available, a new oil system or a heat pump.
## What the Wachusett Reservoir took, and what it left

The reservoir is the town's defining feature. In 1897 the Nashua River was impounded at the Wachusett Dam, and over 2,200 acres of West Boylston's land were used for the reservoir, the most of any town. Many buildings were moved to unaffected parts of town, but the majority were demolished and filled by the reservoir. West Boylston was incorporated in 1808. The town has six entries on the National Register of Historic Places, from the Bigelow Tavern Historic District to the Old Stone Church off Route 140.

The reservoir water is for Boston, and the town gets its own water from two town wells. The town covers 13.8 square miles, 12.9 of them land, and includes the village of Oakdale on the far side of the reservoir along Route 140.
## Apartments, townhouses and rentals

West Boylston has more multi-family housing than the typical town on our list. 538 units (18.4%) are in multi-unit buildings, including 160 in two-unit buildings (5.5%), 95 in buildings of three or four units (3.2%) and 283 in buildings of five or more (9.7%). Attached townhouse units add 353 more (12.0%), and detached houses are 69.6%, which ranks 30th of 50. Renters live in 607 households, 21.2%, which ranks 18th.
Vacancy is low: 68 of the 2,930 units are empty, 2.3%, against 3.6% for the middle town.
## A municipal utility and the rebate rule

West Boylston Municipal Lighting Plant is the town's electric utility, so heat pump rebate rules differ from those in towns served by National Grid. With 1,128 homes on utility gas, a good share of owners may fall into the group that Mass Save serves, while others would look to the Lighting Plant. Our [heat pump page](/cities/west-boylston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) sets out the terms.

faq.q: Do West Boylston homes get Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: Some may. The town has a municipal electric utility, so which program applies depends on how the home is heated. Gas homes and oil, propane or electric homes can land on different paths, and the West Boylston Municipal Lighting Plant is the first call. Confirm Mass Save terms at masssave.com.

faq.q: Is oil or gas more common in West Boylston?
faq.a: They are nearly even. Oil heats 1,173 occupied homes (41.0%) and utility gas heats 1,128 (39.4%). Which one suits your house depends on whether a gas main runs by it, and on the age and condition of your current equipment.

faq.q: Do older West Boylston homes need special sizing?
faq.a: They often do. With a median build year of 1964 and 67.3% of homes built before 1980, insulation and air leakage vary a lot from house to house. The home's heating load is assessed before a system is quoted, so the system fits the house and not the old nameplate.

faq.q: How many West Boylston homes are in apartment buildings?
faq.a: The ACS counts 538 units in multi-unit buildings, 18.4% of the town, including 283 in buildings of five or more. Another 353 are attached townhouse units. Detached houses are 69.6% of the stock. Heating and cooling choices differ between a detached house and a unit in a shared building.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,173 West Boylston homes and utility gas 1,128, so a boiler or furnace replacement is often a choice between like-for-like and switching fuels. Most of the housing predates 1980, which matters for sizing.
body: ## A near tie between two fuels

Fuel oil heats 41.0% of occupied homes, 23rd among the 50 towns, and utility gas heats 39.4%, 26th. Electricity heats 292, tank gas 148, wood 80 and other fuels or coal 41. No single fuel dominates, so the replacement path starts with whatever the house burns now.
### Gas homes

A gas home usually swaps in another gas unit. That work belongs to licensed plumbers and gas fitters, the only people who can pull a gas permit in Massachusetts, and a final inspection normally follows. The building department can confirm how it handles the filing.
### Oil homes

A house on oil has three paths: a new oil boiler or furnace, a conversion to gas if a main is available on the street, or a heat pump. The existing tank and chimney stay in play for the first path only.
### Older houses

West Boylston's median home dates to 1964, and 851 homes come from 1940 through 1959, the largest age band. Heating loops in those houses can outlast the boiler, so the heating load is assessed before a system is quoted instead of copying the old unit. Another 624 homes come from 1960 through 1979 and 497 from 1939 or earlier, so most of the town's equipment sits in houses that predate 1980.
### Renters

With 607 renter households, 21.2%, rentals are a real part of the town. State rules set the floor for a rental unit during the heating season at 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight. The landlord covers heat unless the lease assigns it elsewhere. This is general information, not legal advice.
### A cold-night call

Dial (508) 786-8755 if heat fails after dark. Emergency calls are answered at any hour, and there is no charge for the written estimate that comes before the work. The broader housing numbers are on the [West Boylston page](/cities/west-boylston).

faq.q: Is converting from oil to gas worth it here?
faq.a: Only where a main runs past the property, and about 1,128 homes in town already use gas. Start with the gas company, then set the conversion cost beside a new oil system and a heat pump. The lowest first cost is not always the lowest over the life of the equipment.

faq.q: What about the 80 homes that burn wood?
faq.a: Wood heats 80 West Boylston homes, 2.8%. A stove or wood boiler needs a sound chimney and flue, inspected before the cold season. As a backup to a gas or oil system it can help in an outage, provided it is used safely.

faq.q: When is a new boiler the better call than a repair?
faq.a: One failed part on a younger boiler is usually worth fixing. A cracked heat exchanger, repeated breakdowns or equipment far past its expected life lean toward replacement. A written estimate that shows both routes makes the decision easier.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: West Boylston has 538 units in multi-unit buildings and 353 attached townhouse units beside 2,039 detached houses, so cooling jobs range from condensers in yards to units in shared buildings.
body: ## Cooling a mix of houses and shared buildings

The ACS counts 2,039 detached houses in West Boylston, 69.6% of the stock and 30th of 50. Attached townhouses number 353 (12.0%), and 538 units (18.4%) are in multi-unit buildings. The middle town is 76.7% detached, so West Boylston has a wider mix, and the cooling plan depends on the building type.
### Detached houses

A detached house generally allows an outdoor condenser, and a second one if a separate zone is wanted upstairs. Window units remain an option for a single room, though they block the window. Central cooling then relies on duct runs, which an older house may lack. The median West Boylston home was built in 1964, a year when central air was far from standard in houses.
### Townhouses and shared buildings

Townhouse units, 353 in town, and the 283 units in buildings of five or more may have less outdoor space. A ductless mini-split can fit when a condenser location is limited, but a building's rules and the owner's approval govern where outdoor equipment goes. Check with the owner or association before planning, particularly for units on upper floors.
### Ductless in older houses

A mini-split avoids ducts, so it suits additions, finished attics and rooms that the old system never reached. Because the same equipment can heat in winter, the [heat pump page](/cities/west-boylston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Electric homes and newer builds
Electricity heats 292 West Boylston homes, 10.2%, the 25th-highest share. The 601 homes built since 2000 (20.5%), including 267 since 2010, are likelier to have ducts able to carry cooling.
### Sizing

A unit that is too big cools fast and shuts off before humidity falls, leaving the rooms clammy. Insulation, window area and orientation set the right size, not the old unit. A house with an addition, such as a finished attic, may need its own zone.

faq.q: Can I put an air conditioner in a West Boylston condo or townhouse?
faq.a: Often yes, with a ductless system. Outdoor placement is the main question, because it may need approval from an owner or association, and the refrigerant line has to find a route to the indoor head. A visit shows where the condenser can sit and how the line would run.

faq.q: Is central air worth adding to a mid-century house?
faq.a: Sometimes. The deciding factor is where the ducts would go. If walls and ceilings have to be opened, a ductless system can be the simpler route. West Boylston has 851 homes from 1940 through 1959, the largest band, so the question applies to a big slice of the town.

faq.q: Why is my AC running but the house stays warm?
faq.a: Dirty coils, a failed capacitor, a refrigerant leak or a clogged filter are typical causes. Some are small repairs, while a failed compressor in an old system may call for replacement. Having the estimate in writing separates the two before you spend anything.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: West Boylston has its own Municipal Lighting Plant, so heat pump rebates follow the municipal rule: Mass Save generally covers gas-heated homes, while others look to the Lighting Plant. Oil heats 1,173 homes, gas 1,128.
body: ## Two rebate paths in a municipal town

The Lighting Plant, not National Grid, is the electric utility here, so Mass Save generally reaches only homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and everyone else looks to the Lighting Plant's own program. The [general heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains the Mass Save terms, and the Lighting Plant can describe its own.
### Gas homes

West Boylston's 1,128 gas homes are the group Mass Save is most likely to reach. For them, a heat pump is often considered for cooling and for shoulder-season heating, with the gas appliance kept for cold weather.
### Oil, propane and electric homes

The 1,173 oil homes, 148 propane homes and 292 electric homes would generally look to the Lighting Plant. In each, a heat pump displaces something: delivered oil, tank gas or electric resistance heat. We have no figures for the Lighting Plant's program, so ask it directly before planning around any number.
### Older stock and weatherization

West Boylston's median home was built in 1964, and 1,972 homes, 67.3%, predate 1980, the 11th-highest share. One test in Mass Save's program is being built in 2000 or later, which 601 homes, 20.5%, are. Older houses may need an assessment and some air sealing first.
### Apartments, townhouses and shared systems

With 538 units in multi-unit buildings and 353 in townhouses, many heat pump decisions involve a shared building. Mini-splits are common there because they avoid new ducts, though the owner or association must approve outdoor equipment.
### Water for the system
The reservoir water goes to Boston, and the town draws from two town wells of its own. Heat pumps themselves do not use household water, so the point matters only for a humidifier or a boiler fill.

faq.q: Which utility do I contact about a West Boylston heat pump rebate?
faq.a: Start with the West Boylston Municipal Lighting Plant, which runs its own program. Mass Save may apply if your home heats with gas, so check masssave.com as well. Ask each for current terms, and keep application deadlines in mind, since programs change from year to year.

faq.q: I heat with oil. Can I still get a rebate?
faq.a: Possibly, through the Lighting Plant's program rather than Mass Save. We have no figures for it, so call the utility before relying on any amount. The home may also have to satisfy a weatherization condition, and with 1,972 homes built before 1980, many in town would need an assessment first.

faq.q: Will a heat pump work in a mid-century house?
faq.a: It can, if the heating load is understood and the house is reasonably sealed. A heat pump may carry most of the year, with the existing boiler or furnace kept for the coldest days. The assessment of the home's heating load decides how much it can take, and it matters more than the year the house was built.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: West Boylston splits between 1,173 oil homes and 1,128 gas homes, so tune-ups range from burner cleaning to combustion checks. Rentals are 21.2% of households, which raises the stakes on a cold-night failure.
body: ## Two main fuels, two service routines

Oil systems get a yearly cleaning of the burner, nozzle, filter and heat exchanger, along with a combustion test, while gas systems get a burner, venting and connection check. West Boylston has both in large numbers, along with 148 tank-gas homes, 80 wood homes and 292 electric homes, so a service plan starts with the fuel.
### Oil visit

- Clean the burner and heat exchanger
- Change the nozzle and filter
- Test combustion and look at the flue
### Gas visit

- Check burner and flame
- Inspect venting
- Inspect gas connections and controls
### Wood, tank gas and electric
Wood stoves need a chimney and flue inspection. Tank-gas appliances get the gas checks. Electric and heat pump households need filters, coils and drains cleaned.
### Why age matters

The largest age band is 1940 to 1959, with 851 homes (29.0%), and 624 more come from 1960 through 1979. Piping and distribution in those houses can be older than the boiler, so a service visit is a chance to spot leaks, rust or tired valves.
### Landlords and tenants

Renters occupy 607 West Boylston households. A boiler serviced ahead of the heating season is less likely to fail in the first cold week, and owners of multi-unit buildings, 538 units in town, have more households depending on one system.
### Heat pumps and cooling equipment

The 292 electric-heat homes, and any home with a heat pump or air conditioner, need filters cleaned through the busy seasons, coils checked once a year and the outdoor unit kept clear of leaves, snow and ice. A drain that clogs can leave water around an indoor head, so a quick look each spring is cheap insurance.
### Small landlords

Two-unit buildings number 160 units in West Boylston and three- or four-unit buildings 95. An owner living in one unit and renting out the others can service one boiler for the whole house, and a single yearly visit covers every household.
### Calendar

Heating checks suit late summer or early fall, and cooling checks suit spring. Call at any time for new noises, a smell of oil or smoke, or short cycling. For the air side of the house, see the [air quality page](/cities/west-boylston/indoor-air-quality).

faq.q: How often should my West Boylston oil boiler be cleaned?
faq.a: Yearly, before the heating season starts. Soot builds up on the heat exchanger over time and can cut efficiency or bring on a breakdown. A late-summer visit leaves time for a replacement part to arrive before cold weather. Oil is the fuel of 41.0% of town households.

faq.q: Do gas furnaces need annual service as well?
faq.a: Yes, it is a sound habit. The technician checks the burner, venting, controls and gas connections, and reports what is worn. West Boylston has 1,128 gas homes, so this is the second most common fuel group for service in town, a hair behind oil.

faq.q: I own a three-unit building. Does service differ?
faq.a: The checks are the same, but a failure affects more households at once. West Boylston has 160 units in two-unit buildings and 95 in buildings of three or four units. Servicing each boiler yearly protects every household that relies on it.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: West Boylston's housing runs from 497 homes built in 1939 or earlier to 267 since 2010, and 538 units share walls in multi-unit buildings, so air concerns differ by building type as well as age.
body: ## Air across old, mid-century and newer housing

By the ACS 2022 counts, West Boylston has 497 homes (17.0%) from 1939 or earlier, 851 (29.0%) from 1940 to 1959, 624 (21.3%) from 1960 to 1979, 357 (12.2%) from 1980 to 1999 and 601 (20.5%) from 2000 on. A house can mix eras, since additions often differ from the original building.
### Older houses

Older houses often leak around windows, sills and attic floors. Those gaps can dilute some pollutants while admitting dust, pollen and basement damp. Before renovating a very old house, a qualified specialist should test for lead paint or asbestos. The 497 homes built in 1939 or earlier and 851 built from 1940 through 1959 together are nearly half the stock.
### Tighter newer houses

Tightness is likelier in the 267 homes built since 2010, 9.1% of the stock. In such a house, humidity, cooking fumes and furniture off-gassing linger unless fresh air arrives, so exhaust fans that vent outdoors do real work.
### Shared buildings

With 538 units in multi-unit buildings, 18.4% of the town, some residents share walls or hallways. Cooking odors and smoke can travel between units, and one unit's ventilation fan can affect another's air. Sealing gaps and keeping exhaust fans working help.
### Humidity and water

Winter heating can dry indoor air, and summer brings humidity back. A humidifier or dehumidifier helps, but a humidifier draws water, and West Boylston gets its water from two town wells, so mineral buildup depends on what the supply carries.
### Filters and ducts

A denser filter only helps when the blower can still move air through it, so confirm that first, and replace it on the schedule the maker gives. Cleaning ducts is a job for visible dirt or mold, and not a yearly chore. See the [tune-up page](/cities/west-boylston/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) for the mechanical side.

faq.q: Is the air in an older West Boylston house worse?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Older houses leak, so fresh air gets in, but so do dust and damp. Newer houses are tight and hold in moisture and fumes. Either can be improved once the source is found, and the fix is rarely the same for both kinds of house.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not as a routine. Mold, heavy dirt or a renovation that stirred up dust are the usual reasons, and a good many systems never need it. A look at the whole system, filter and returns included, shows whether cleaning would help or whether a better filter fit would do more.

faq.q: Can an apartment have its own air quality problems?
faq.a: Yes. Shared walls and hallways let odors and smoke travel, and a unit without good exhaust ventilation can hold humidity. Working bath and kitchen fans and a filter that fits the system are the first steps, and where the building owns the equipment, the owner or manager has to be part of the fix.
